Level 3: Component architecture

SPD chip

A tiny chip that tells the computer what kind of memory is installed.

What is it?

Serial Presence Detect is a small memory chip on the stick. On DDR5 it is an “SPD hub” that also reads a temperature sensor.

What does it do?

At start-up, the firmware reads it to learn the stick’s size, speed and timings, including XMP or EXPO overclocking profiles.

Why it matters

Without SPD, the firmware would have to guess the memory settings, and the computer might not start.

Real chip

Key specifications

Interface

capacity, speed, timings, voltage
Size

How it connects

  • BIOS chipReads this chip at start-up
  • RAM slotsWhere the stick plugs in

Fun fact

DDR5 moved memory voltage regulation onto the stick itself, using a small power management chip (PMIC).
